long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Leningrad, Igor Sechin studied French and Portuguese at Leningrad State University. His language training took him abroad as an interpreter before he joined the municipal administration in St Petersburg. He later moved into Russia's federal executive administration, progressing through senior staff roles and serving as deputy prime minister with responsibility for industrial and energy policy.

Sechin returned to Rosneft in 2012 and leads the oil producer as chief executive and chairman of its management board. His work there has remained concentrated on energy strategy, industrial policy and the administration of a large operating company. The continuity from government oversight of industry to company leadership defines his public career, while his early language training marks the less conventional route by which it began.

He was Russia's Deputy Prime Minister in Vladimir Putin's cabinet until May 21, 2012, and he is now the CEO, President, and Chairman of the Management Board of Rosneft, the Russian national oil firm.
